claims.statement: frontend/mcm-app/server.js is the BFF's production entrypoint: a CommonJS Express adapter that requires @expo/server/adapter/express, hands the exported dist/server bundle to createRequestHandler, and serves dist/client as static assets; because it runs outside the Metro bundle it cannot require anything from src/, which is why scheduled work reaches the bundle through a loopback HTTP call instead of a function call.

server.js pre-seeds `globalThis.__ExpoImportMetaRegistry = { url: pathToFileURL(__filename).href }` before createRequestHandler loads the bundle, because Metro rewrites `import.meta.url` in bundled dependencies to `globalThis.__ExpoImportMetaRegistry.url` and the exported @expo/server runtime — unlike the Metro dev server — never populates that registry; the `if (!globalThis.__ExpoImportMetaRegistry)` guard is intentional so a future @expo/server version that populates it makes the line a no-op rather than being clobbered.

Without the registry seeding, any bundled dependency calling `createRequire(import.meta.url)` — @copilotkit/runtime's lazily-required adapter on the /bff-api/agent/run path — throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'url')` asynchronously inside the streaming respond pipeline, so the route's own try/catch never sees it: the client hangs with no 500 and no log line, in the container only.

The same lazy require is a build-time consequence: because the specifier is a bare string passed to createRequire(globalThis.__ExpoImportMetaRegistry.url), a static closure walk cannot see it, so the BFF image build re-derives the dynamic specifiers from the freshly exported dist/server and fails when one is not accounted for in the prune script's known-specifier map.

Under express 5 (path-to-regexp v8) the Expo catch-all must be the named, braced route `'/{*splat}'`: a bare `'*'` is rejected at BOOT with `Missing parameter name at index 1: *` while routes are being registered, so the process never reaches app.listen, and the braces make the wildcard optional so `/` itself still matches.

The catch-all uses `app.all` rather than `app.use` deliberately: a route decodes its params, so a malformed percent-encoded path such as `/bff-api/%E0%A4%A` is answered 400 by express before the Expo handler sees it, and the single registration forwards every method and the raw query string (bracket syntax included) for both the /bff-api API surface and the SSR pages.

Static serving selects between two express.static instances on the last DECODED segment of the request path (a dotfile-last path goes to the default `ignore` instance, everything else to a `dotfiles: 'allow'` one), and an undecodable path falls to the strict instance — so a dotfile inside a dot-directory is not served, `/%2Eenv` counts as a dotfile because send decodes before it checks, and files inside dot-directories are served.

serve-static 2 (express 5) changed the `dotfiles` default to ignore files INSIDE a dot-directory as well, which would silently 404 the 45 dependency-shipped assets `expo export` writes under `dist/client/assets/node_modules/.pnpm/…` — the Outfit brand fonts and expo-router's icons — so express 4's rule (ignore only a path whose last segment is a dotfile) is deliberately reproduced by the two-instance selection.

Two suites boot the real `server.js` in a child process through one shared `node -r` preload, and together they are the only tests that exercise the express hosting layer: `tests/unit/bff-server-adapter.test.ts` (the pin for the catch-all, param decoding, static serving and the header middleware) and `tests/unit/bff-server-trust-proxy.test.ts` (the pin for the `trust proxy` origin behaviour). Each copies the real `server.js` and `web-security-headers.js` into a temp directory beside a fixture `dist/client` and replaces only `@expo/server/adapter/express` via `tests/unit/fixtures/expo-adapter-stub.cjs`, a `Module._load` hook whose stub handler echoes what express delivered to the handler plus the request origin exactly as the real adapter builds it (`${req.protocol}://${req.get('host')}`, added for spec 083 T010) in an `X-Test-Origin` response header. `express` resolves from the package's own `node_modules` via `NODE_PATH`, so the version under test is the declared one; the unit tier imports TS modules and the integration tier calls route handlers, and both bypass `server.js`.

No other test would catch the font-serving regression: tests/e2e/web/font-fallback.spec.ts deliberately aborts every web-font request and asserts the app still renders on the system fallback, so it passes whether or not the real fonts are servable from dist/client.

CopilotKit's React Native runtime issues its /bff-api/agent/run request through its own XMLHttpRequest-based streaming-fetch polyfill, which never passes through the axios token-refresh interceptor, so an expired short-lived `mcm_access_token` cookie 401s the run with no refresh attempted; the cookie rides along only because React Native's XMLHttpRequest defaults `withCredentials` to true — the polyfill does not set init.credentials, so a future RN or CopilotKit upgrade that changes that default breaks cookie delivery silently, with the Android E2E harness as the intended regression net.

src/utils/agent-fetch-refresh.ts wraps `globalThis.fetch` once (idempotently, no-op where fetch is unavailable) so that a 401 on the agent run route triggers silentRefresh() followed by a single retry with the fresh cookie; the wrapper is installed by the assistant polyfill loader — the first import in app/_layout.tsx — before CopilotKit issues any run, and CopilotKit resolves fetch at call time.

A second, distinct recovery in the same wrapper handles a THROWN transport error on the agent route only: it waits RUN_RETRY_DELAY_MS (250 ms) for a reset tunnel to re-establish and retries exactly once, which is safe because a dropped connection aborts the upstream gateway turn via @expo/server's AbortController, making the cut turn idempotent-on-failure; non-agent throws propagate unchanged and a genuine 4xx returns a Response so it is never retried.

Neither recovery loops: a still-401 response after a successful refresh is returned as-is, a failed refresh returns the original 401 with no retry, and a second consecutive throw is propagated — so the 401 path and the transport-drop path are each capped at one retry, and createRefreshingFetch is a pure factory taking an injected baseFetch + refresh so both paths are unit-tested without any global.

assistant-polyfills.native.ts is ordered so the refresh wrapper is installed after the CopilotKit crypto and streaming polyfills and before any CopilotKit run — the crypto polyfill, then @copilotkit/react-native/polyfills, then installAgentFetchRefresh() — and its `require` calls are deliberately inline rather than hoisted imports so the LogBox ignore for the crypto polyfill's import-time warning is registered first; the order must not be changed.

The web and native assistant-polyfill loaders are deliberately split at the platform boundary for bundle size: the unsuffixed assistant-polyfills.ts is the web variant and installs ONLY the refresh wrapper (the crypto/streaming globals are native on web), while assistant-polyfills.native.ts loads the polyfill libraries — whose static requires otherwise put text-encoding (535 KB) and web-streams-polyfill (61 KB) in the entry chunk for every web user even though they can never execute there.

Verification of the refresh-retry chain is split by tier: the client-side orchestration over a real mid-session expiry rests on the Android harness, while the server half is proven by the web E2E tests/e2e/web/agent-session-refresh.spec.ts, which drops only the access cookie, observes the `no_token` 401 the agent route sees, and shows POST /bff-api/auth/refresh rotating the cookie so the retry succeeds.

The `@expo/server` express adapter builds every request URL as `${req.protocol}://${req.get('host')}${req.url}`. In production TLS terminates at the edge proxy and a tunnel reaches `server.js` over plain HTTP, so before the fix `req.protocol` read `http` and the two routes that derive an OAuth callback from `new URL(req.url).origin` — the backup consent callback and the account-deletion re-authentication callback (feature 076) — sent Keycloak an unregistered `http://` redirect_uri, which Keycloak refused with `Invalid parameter: redirect_uri` (measured in production 2026-10-25, item 843). CI and dev never saw it because there the BFF serves HTTPS itself on `:8443`, which is why the behaviour is pinned by a unit suite that boots the real `server.js` rather than by the web E2E run.

The fix is `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`, applied at boot above the routes and only when `TRUSTED_PROXY === 'true'`. A numeric value compiles to a hop-count predicate over the socket hop index, so `1` trusts exactly the immediate peer (the tunnel) and nothing wider — the narrowest form that still describes a one-hop deployment, where `true` would trust any peer including a directly connecting client and an address list or CIDR would have to be maintained. Gating it on the env var is what keeps the setting from ever being stronger than the deployment actually is.

Only the SCHEME can move when `trust proxy` is enabled: it makes `req.protocol` honour a trusted hop's `X-Forwarded-Proto`, but the adapter calls `req.get('host')`, a raw `Host` header read with no proxy logic, so `X-Forwarded-Host` cannot change the origin a callback is derived from. The suite pins this directly — a request with `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.test` still yields the origin built from the raw `Host`.

Unset must stay unset, and unset is the default: `TRUSTED_PROXY` defaults to `false` in `src/config/env.ts`, so a directly exposed BFF keeps ignoring a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-Proto` and cannot be talked into believing it serves `https`. The same variable has a second, independent consumer inside the bundle — the rate-limit client identity that `extractClientIp` derives from the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` hop (feature 009, finding #4) — so setting `trust proxy` in `server.js` does not change rate-limit identity, and `extractClientIp` does not change the scheme.
